outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity and enterprise software, led by CrowdStrike, Okta, and Salesforce
strongest.reason: post-earnings beats and raised guidance sparked a sector-wide re-rating, with the IGV software ETF up about 6% and previously lagging names like Zscaler and SentinelOne catching a roughly 10% bid

strongest.area: AI chip and infrastructure complex, led by Nvidia, Marvell, and Micron
strongest.reason: Nvidia's guide to roughly 70% FY28 revenue growth pulled the broader semiconductor and neocloud trade higher, with SMH/SOXX up 3-3.5% and CoreWeave/Nebius gaining 6-7% in premarket trading

weakest.area: AMD and Arm within the chip complex
weakest.reason: both eased back even as most semiconductor peers extended Thursday's Nvidia-driven rally, a divergence worth watching for signs of profit-taking after a strong run

weakest.area: Treasuries and the dollar heading into Friday's Jackson Hole speech
weakest.reason: yields and the dollar index have stayed firm as roughly 1-in-3 odds of a September rate hike keep a lid on risk appetite in rate-sensitive corners of the market

outlook.nextStep: Friday's Jackson Hole keynote from Fed Chair Warsh is the single biggest near-term catalyst and is probably better watched than acted on until there's clarity on tone, especially since he's broken from the tradition of pre-signaling policy. The broadening software and chip rally is worth a closer look for signs of whether it holds beyond the initial earnings pop or fades as attention shifts to next week's data.

signals.title: Cybersecurity sector re-rates sharply as CrowdStrike and Okta beat and raise
signals.body: CrowdStrike posted its best day ever, surging roughly 20% after fiscal Q2 revenue of $1.47B (up 26% YoY) and EPS beat expectations, while Okta jumped nearly 29% on its own AI-driven security demand. The rally spread to previously lagging names, with Zscaler and SentinelOne both up about 10% and the CIBR cybersecurity ETF gaining roughly 7% versus QQQ's under-1% move.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this marks a durable re-rating of the group or a short-covering-driven bounce in previously weak names

signals.title: Enterprise software rally broadens beyond Salesforce
signals.body: The iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF (IGV) jumped about 6%, led by a roughly 22% gain in Okta, 20% in Salesforce, and 18% in CrowdStrike. ServiceNow rose about 10% to close at $138.43, and Snowflake traded higher in sympathy. Salesforce leadership publicly pushed back on 'SaaSpocalypse' narratives, arguing agentic AI adoption is fueling demand rather than disrupting the business.
signals.focus: worth watching whether the broader software group can hold these gains once the earnings-driven excitement fades

signals.title: AI chip rally extends as Marvell, Micron, and neocloud names join Nvidia's move
signals.body: Following Nvidia's earnings beat, Marvell gained about 5.8% and Micron added roughly 4.5%, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF up 3.5%. Neocloud infrastructure names also rallied, with Nebius and CoreWeave up around 7% and 6% respectively in premarket trading.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether the neocloud strength signals genuine AI-capex acceleration or is more momentum-driven

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote lands Friday with rate odds split
signals.body: July inflation ran at 3.4%, still well above the Fed's 2% target, and traders currently price roughly 1-in-3 odds of a rate hike at the September 16 meeting. Warsh, three months into the job, has broken from the tradition of pre-signaling policy at Jackson Hole, leaving markets with less visibility than usual into his likely tone.
signals.focus: probably better watched than acted on until the speech itself provides real clarity

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ether extend gains on ETF inflows and a broad crypto upswing
signals.body: Bitcoin pushed back toward its recent highs near $81,000 while Ethereum broke out further above $2,500, both up roughly 3% as the total crypto market cap climbed to about $2.68T. Ether's move was helped by around $180M in ETF inflows.
signals.focus: worth watching whether inflows continue or this proves to be a bounce within the recent trading range

signals.title: Robotics stays choppy day to day even as the multi-quarter buildout narrative holds
signals.body: Tesla continued to build on its robotaxi approvals in Nevada alongside Uber and Waymo, while UBTECH ticked modestly higher in Hong Kong trading after cooling from this week's China humanoid-robotics rally. The broader robotics and automation group is up roughly 12% over the past year, with Nvidia's robotics division cited as a key growth driver across the space.
signals.focus: worth treating single-day swings in individual robotics names as noise relative to the longer-term capital-flow trend into the space
